author: Riskayyy
body:
Hi!
Next week, there is a staff meeting being held on Teamspeak and we're looking for some topics to talk about! Of course, we have plenty already, but what would you like us to talk about in the meeting? (Michael gave me permission to make this thread FYI)

Suggested topics:
- General Lag issues.
- Leaderboard for Teams.
- Official Scrims. 
- Advertisement.
- Jr.Map Developer rank and its validity. 
- Staff training
- More gamemodes (Capture the Flag)
- Second tournament. 
- Senior Staff's response time with regards to appeals.
- Media page (avicus.net/live)
- Easy player search box (to avoid use of game tab)
- Voting system (top voter earns extra credits or potentially gold for 1 month)
- Total credit count (showing the totality of credits earned)
- Birthdays (?) (Assuming alerts or something alike)
- Clean up and update forum guidelines
- Emphasis on in-game announcements
- Credit bonus for joining the forums
- Public build server of affiliate w/ trusted build servers
- Disabling auto-refresh of the game selectors

Thanks in advance!

replies.author: ImRaging
replies.body:
One more thing :P

The staff team need to cut down on the 'grey area' of the rules. There are so many decisions based on someone's opinion, that it can get confusing knowing what is right and what is wrong.

A good example is spawn killing. There are many interpretations of what is spawn killing, and what isn't. One mod may say that killing a player inside of their spawn, at all, is spawn killing. Some say that you can give the player a certain amount of time before killing them, no matter where they are. Another may say, that in order to be following the rules, you must not touch the player until they are a certain distance away from spawn. This is just one example.

Everyone knows that the 'grey area' can't be washed away completely, but it can certainly be cut down so it's smaller.

replies.author: Dipper_1332
replies.body:
Issues to discuss:
At the beginning of each meeting Keenan should inform the staff when it comes to statistics about Avicus.
 
Statistics will help Keenan and the staff team see the bigger goal when it comes to moderating in order to improve the server. 

Statistics should be stated but they should obviously be stated in context, eg. a decrease in players due to school starting again for the northern hemisphere is just seasonal.
Through this the staff as a team can tackle constraints that may be stunting the growth of the server.

Statistics: Server growth in terms of the overall playtime of players in a set period of time, the amount of new players and possibly other statistics such as the amount of reports/bug complaints that could mean extra moderating for the staff. 
(Note: If Avicus is not receiving a large amount of income, ways to increase the server profit should be dealt with and spoken about)

This may not seem attractive to Keenan or the higher staff, due to the possibility of Avicus decreasing when it comes to growth. It may affect the staff negatively; they may feel the server is a lost cause. It may also affect the staff positively; they may feel they need to do their duties better than ever to keep the server alive. This may also cost Keenan time when it comes to tracking these statistics, but without properly viewing and managing statistics how will Keenan/anyone know if the server is really doing successfully.

I won't go into detail, but here is essentially what we discussed in this weeks meeting:

- Lag issues Certainly a point where we all agreed on.

- Staff training system  
- Moderators gaining access with //drain 
- Leaving threads and how to deal with them Certainly a point of weakness we all wanted to discuss.
- Moderators handling their own appeals. :) I guess we're just waiting for the confirmation from the senior staff. 

Other topics were discussed, but they were just brushed upon unlike the other topics :)
